evidence:
NESTING (static, holds). task.toml:18 [agent].timeout_sec=7200.0; task.toml:21 build_timeout_sec=600.0; task.toml:27 [verifier].timeout_sec=13200.0. tests/test.sh:213 `run_suite gates 1500`; tests/test.sh:224 `run_suite scored 11100`; tests/test.sh:207 runs rewardkit under `timeout "$budget_sec"` with `--max-concurrent-agent 1` (judges sequential). Judge timeouts (judge.toml:4 in each): gates/render 600, gates/constraints 600, scored/functional 9000, scored/polish 900, scored/visual 900. Arithmetic: each gate judge 600 < 1500 and sequential sum 600+600=1200 < 1500 (300 s slack); each scored judge <= 9000 < 11100 and sequential sum 9000+900+900=10800 < 11100 (300 s slack); budgets 1500+11100=12600 < 13200 (600 s slack); internal-sheet form 'sum of judges < verifier': 1200+10800=12000 < 13200. Liveness: test.sh:116-121 start probe 120 x 0.25 s = 30 s plus 2 s per-URL urlopen timeout (test.sh:50); restart helper probe 120 x 0.25 s = 30 s (test.sh:171-176) inside the 55 s restart_mcp.py HELPER_TIMEOUT_SEC (tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:11); all fit in the 600 s verifier slack. All of these values and tests/test.sh are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff of test.sh: identical; task.toml differs only in identity/metadata lines 5-7, 10-12, 14-15), so no unauthorised timeout change was made, consistent with REVIEW_POLICY 'Keep canonical budgets'. Build: environment/Dockerfile is identical to the template (node:22-bookworm-slim, one apt layer, global express + better-sqlite3), plausibly well under 600 s but no cold-build timing is recorded.

ADEQUACY ('long enough') is NOT MEASURED. The functional judge must grade 40 criteria in one batched 9000 s session (225 s per criterion on average, including the single-use real process restart and criteria that wait on the five-second execution limit), on z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx through claude-code + Playwright MCP; polish has 6 criteria in 900 s (150 s each); visual 3 likert criteria in 900 s. The template these budgets were sized against ships 2 functional / 4 polish / 6 visual placeholder criteria, so the canonical 9000 s is not evidence for a 40-criterion workload. raw-evidence-index.json states its scope is 'Scripted golden behaviour evidence only. Not a configured LLM judge run' and lists 'Visual ratings, judge duration, Oracle reward and reward discrimination are not measured'; its hashes verify, but scripted Playwright duration is not judge duration (REVIEW_POLICY: 'Workload is measured, not inferred from a timeout number'). No agent-run timing exists for the 7200 s agent budget against a hard custom-editor build either. Per the skill ('Never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass') the nesting half passes and the sufficiency half remains an open, required measurement; this is an evidence gap, not a demonstrated defect.
counterexample: Not demonstrated, risk only: a fully conforming app whose functional judge needs more than 9000 s for the 40 batched criteria would hit the judge timeout (or `timeout 11100` at test.sh:224 -> `exit 0` with the earlier zero/gate-only record), attributing a harness workload failure to the submission. Conversely nothing in the nesting lets a broken app gain credit from a timeout: every timeout path leaves the zero reward.
suggested_fix: Do not change any timeout now. Run one full configured verifier pass of the golden on these exact bytes (claude-code + z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx), record per-judge wall-clock for gates/render, gates/constraints, functional, polish and visual plus cold image build time, and bind the logs into raw-evidence-index.json. If functional exceeds roughly 75% of 9000 s, reduce redundant browser work/criteria together with public scope, or request an explicitly authorised, recorded budget change (below five hours total) that keeps 9000-class judge < scored budget and gates + scored < verifier.
